title.title: Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension nine
title.subtitle: Claim: the rank-one projectors $uu^\top$, $u \in \mathbb R^4$, cannot be cut into 10 pieces of smaller diameter

plain: Can every shape be cut into a few pieces, each narrower than the whole? This 9D one needs more than 10

beats.text: Borsuk, 1933: can every bounded set in $\mathbb R^d$ be cut into $d+1$ smaller pieces?
Kahn and Kalai said no in dimension 1325. By May 2026 the record was 63
The claim: lines through the origin of $\mathbb R^4$ need more than 10 pieces

steps: Then perpendicular lines would always get different labels
A parity count forces those labels into one rigid pattern
A finite, Lean-checked search finds no such pattern

achievement.note: The least failing dimension is now somewhere between 4 and 9

verify.detail: Compact, diameter $\sqrt 2$, no cover by ten smaller sets; 145 generated case files
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: The lowest known failure was dimension sixty three. Now: lines through the origin of four-space.
Ten smaller pieces would force a labelling pattern, and a checked search finds none.
Claimed: Borsuk fails from dimension nine.

sources.quote: Then Max Grinsztajn, assisted by GPT-5.5 Pro, dimension 63 (321-point three-distance set; arXiv 2608.12561, Wikipedia dates it May 2026)
then 63 in 2026 (Grinsztajn with GPT-5.5 Pro, arXiv 2608.12561)
cannot be covered by 10 sets of diameter < √2
It does not find the smallest failing dimension, which is now somewhere between 4 and 9
That analysis is in Lean as 145 generated case files
